# The Stars That Travel Together

## Scripture

*"Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell me, if you understand. Who marked off its dimensions? Surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it? On what were its footings set, or who laid its cornerstone—while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?"* — Job 38:4-7 (NIV)

## Reflection

Step outside on a clear November evening and look toward the eastern horizon. You may notice a loose cluster of stars—the Pleiades—but look closer and you'll find something more remarkable: the Hyades, a V-shaped gathering of stars that travel together through our galaxy. These stars share not only a birthplace but a common motion, drifting through space as a family, bound by gravity's gentle pull.

Job's ancient question rings across the centuries: "Where were you when the morning stars sang together?" God reminds Job—and us—that creation's foundations were laid before any human witness. Yet here's the wonder: those distant stars, traveling together for billions of years, were singing before we existed. They still sing.

We often feel like solitary wanderers, charting our own courses through life's darkness. But the Hyades remind us that God designed companionship into the fabric of creation itself. We're not meant to drift alone. Like those stars, we're called to move together—sharing light, sharing purpose, sharing the long journey home.

## Prayer

Father, thank You for the stars that travel together, reminding us that we were made for community. When we feel isolated or adrift, draw us back to the fellowship of believers who share our path. Let our shared light point others toward You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
